answer.exemplar: The absolute value of x is the distance from x to zero, so |x| < 4 asks for the points closer than 4 units from the origin, and those points form the single connected interval from -4 to 4, described with and. The inequality |x| > 4 asks for points farther than 4 units away, and those split into two disconnected pieces, x < -4 and x > 4, which must be joined with or. In general |x| < a gives -a < x < a while |x| > a gives x < -a or x > a.
